Tuesday Labs opens reservations for Voxel home robot at an estimated $20,000

The refundable $200 reservation targets US delivery in 2028, while substantial prototype redesign remains ahead.

Humanoids Daily ↗20 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 4Videos 1

Reservations precede the finished product

New York-based Tuesday Labs, led by former Boston Dynamics roboticist Ros Shinkle, introduced Voxel Series-1. A $200 reservation is refundable before an order is placed. The estimated $20,000 price is not final; deliveries in selected US areas are expected in 2028 but could come later.

A proposed household helper

Voxel is intended to put belongings away, report where it last saw an item, fetch objects and water plants. The published design has seven-degree-of-freedom arms, actuated wrists, one-degree-of-freedom grippers, Z-shaped legs and stereo RGB cameras. No unfamiliar-home success rate or human-assistance requirement has been established.

Hardware remains subject to redesign

The reservation terms describe the imagery and demonstrations as a concept and development prototype. A substantial hardware redesign is expected, so appearance, capabilities and specifications may change. An edition number does not guarantee delivery priority; this is an early reservation launch for a developing product.
